title: Antoine de Bordeaux (London) to Brienne, 30 May 1653 NS, BL Add MS 4200 ff. 88-90 (Thurloe intercept)

documents.shelfmark: BL Add MS 4200 ff. 88-90 (DECODE R8390; duplicates R8391, R8393)

plaintext.source: No decipherment of the letter exists. The English Deciphering Branch's key sheet for 'Mr. Bordeaux' 1653 (BL Add MS 32263 f. 1, DECODE R7537) is a key, not a plaintext; it was the source of the reading.

transcription.source: Tomokiyo's provisional transcription (810 tokens, 156 symbols), corrected against DECODE page images
transcription.notes: The provisional transcription merged two glyphs and dropped diacritics; that alone defeated the ciphertext-only solver.

system.summary: Letters as graphic signs and plain numbers 15-37; three diacritic-marked number series (prime, two dots, overbar) are alphabetical CV syllabaries with common words embedded; a few name codes.

diacritics.note: Prime, two dots and overbar on numbers select the syllable series; the clerk often omits them.

system.doubled_letters: ll is a sign of its own
system.sibling_key: Brienne's Cipher 2 (1651) and Lasry's key for Mazarin to Bordeaux (1654): same design, different values. Used for the design hypothesis only.
system.notes: 14 unread: name codes 25‾ 28‾ 43‾ 332 344 396‾ and the rare tokens 6¨ 10 30' 35' 68' 98 14' 46¨.

prior_solution.where: English Deciphering Branch key sheet, BL Add MS 32263 f. 1 (DECODE R7537)

conditions.human_role: Supplied the DECODE login (session cookie) for the key sheet and page images.
tools: simulated annealing with monotone syllabary alignment (solver.py)

solution.what: Symbol classes, token counts and IC (0.019) on the provisional transcription.
Design A from sibling keys of the same office: marked series are alphabetical syllabaries, overbar and three-digit groups are nomenclature.
Plaintext sought in Birch (Thurloe SP i) and Guizot's despatches; 30 May 1653 in neither. Found DECODE R7537, the English key for 'Mr. Bordeaux' 1653.
Solver recovers 99 % on design-A controls of equal length; 52 % and 9 % when 10 % of diacritics are misread.
Ciphertext-only annealing on the real text, 21+ seeds over series orders and unit lists.
Transcribed key sheet R7537; it confirms design A exactly.
Checked the page images: 21 corrections, two merged glyphs split, lost marks restored.
Applied the key plus context-derived additions; letter read except name codes and rare tokens.
Duplicate of the ending (R8391) agrees token for token; content fits the Ormée negotiations of May 1653.

Correction after an outside check of the write-up: the page's English for the first cipher sentence ('Ce n'est pas que si nos affaires estoyent plus florissantes nous n'eussions sujet de tesmoigner quelque mescontentement...') read 'Even if our affairs were more flourishing, we would still have reason to show some displeasure', which blurs the logic; after 'ce n'est pas que' the lone 'ne' is a full negation, so it is 'Not that, were our affairs more flourishing, we would lack cause to show some displeasure' (France has the grievance but cannot afford to show it). Page paraphrase and context paragraph corrected; the French decipherment is unchanged.

Credit corrected under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): Lasry's 2025 solution is of item B (1654), a different key that does not read item A (1653); his credit here changed from 'prior solution' to 'pointer' (the key design his item-B key showed). Item B is not a document of this entry.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): R8390: transcription ct2.txt (corrected) and ciphertext.txt (Tomokiyo's, normalised), decryption plaintext_1653.txt; key_file key_work.txt (R7537 sheet + context additions) and key7537.txt (the sheet as transcribed).

Gold-standard pilot (Lasry's advice, 20 Nov 2026): f. 88r cut into 5 deskewed bands, 238 candidate boxes; blind Fable 5.2 first pass (222 signs, 94 types; 13 split, 40 part, 16 junk, 8 missed); Claude Opus 5.5 corrected boxes and types in CTTS 3.7.0 by computer use (43 min + 5 min review + 13 min validation fixes). Final 224 signs, 83 types; first pass 28.1 % sign error box by box, 3.6 % with its own notes; first CTTS pass 4.0 %. Against ct2: 219 of 223 tokens agree; differences 96 single bar (ct2 96=), one 63 without prime, 3 96‾ (ct2 396‾), ?52' doubtful under the stain (ct2 52' from R8393): candidate corrections to ct2, not made. Model-made, checked against ct2: not yet a human gold standard.
A person checked the final CTTS sign table of f. 88r (reported by the user; checker not named): correct except ?52', the sign under the stain at the head of band 3, which stays unconfirmed.

texts.label: R8390, 30 May 1653, BL Add MS 4200 ff. 88-90
texts.summary: Bordeaux reports that the Council heard the Bordeaux (Ormée) deputies through two commissioners before Cromwell ("le General") gave him his audience, and that the treaty agreed after the Parliament's resolutions is still unsigned. England may help Bordeaux indirectly, so Brienne should hold back the offer of French mediation; English fear that a France rid of sedition would back the Stuart party could push Cromwell against French interests. ct2.txt is the transcription corrected here against the page images; ciphertext.txt is Tomokiyo's provisional transcription as normalised.
